items.title: Rokid Glasses 2 launch with upgraded design, bigger battery, and Dolby Audio support
items.rationale: New hardware: Rokid's second-gen microLED display glasses add AI-agent support, a bigger battery, and a lighter frame, and are pitched directly at Meta Ray-Ban Display. This one card covers the Rokid cluster.
items.excerpt: Rokid has launched a second-gen model of its smart glasses with a microLED display. The new glasses have a more comfortable design, a bigger battery capacity, upgraded audio, and support for AI agents.

items.title: Raycast's new iOS keyboard app lets you dictate, swipe type and use AI commands without switching apps
items.rationale: New release: Raycast ships a full iPhone keyboard with swipe typing, dictation, and AI writing commands built in, so you can run AI rewrites inside any app without switching keyboards.
items.excerpt: Raycast's new iPhone keyboard combines swipe typing, AI writing tools, voice dictation, GIF search, and text shortcuts. You can now access its productivity features without switching keyboards.

items.title: Google's new Android XR tools let developers test apps without needing to buy expensive smart glasses
items.rationale: New tooling from Android Dev Summit: developers can build and test smart-glasses apps in an emulator without owning the hardware, and Android CLI gains hooks that let AI coding agents test apps and find performance problems.
items.excerpt: At the 2026 Android Dev Summit, Google has announced some interesting features coming to both Android XR and Android CLI. Developers can now build and test apps for smart glasses without owning the hardware, while Android's command-line tools are getting upgrades that help AI coding agents test applications and identify performance problems.

items.title: Strava adds Google Gemini integration with personalized workout insights
items.rationale: New integration: Strava subscribers can now connect Gemini and get personalized insights drawn from their workout history, which brings wearable fitness data into a general-purpose assistant.
items.excerpt: Strava expanded its AI integrations with Google Gemini this week, allowing subscribers to get personalized insights based on their workout history.

items.title: Google Home update should make Gemini stop saying 'Sorry, I didn't understand' so much
items.rationale: New release: the latest Gemini for Home update targets a bug where speakers randomly say 'I didn't understand', plus other fixes. It is a fresh release in the running Gemini-on-speakers rollout.
items.excerpt: Google's latest Gemini for Home update targets a few issues, like one where speakers randomly blurt out "I didn't understand"...

https://9to5google.com/2026/10/29/google.new_action: New Gemini for Home software release (late October) fixing the random 'Sorry, I didn't understand' responses. The 10-02 card covered the earlier September noise-handling update.
